speaker: alice
text: Right, so here's something that'll blow your mind from the Mediterranean. <cite index="9-9,9-10,9-11">After Marseille brought in stronger environmental regulations back in the 80s, Neptune seagrass has bounced back at exceptional rates - not through replanting, but just by removing the pollutants that caused the problem in the first place</cite>. Talk about letting nature do the heavy lifting!

speaker: charlie
text: That's brilliant, and it gets better. <cite index="15-15,15-16">Over in Scotland's Cairngorms, they've released more than 35 wildcats since 2023, and we're already seeing success with seven litters born in 2024 and five more in 2025</cite>. These little legends were on the brink but now they're making a proper comeback.

speaker: alice
text: <cite index="12-3,12-4,12-5">But here's the real game-changer - scientists have won a major prize for work on mycorrhizal fungi, those underground networks that connect plant roots and pull down around 13 billion tons of CO2 each year</cite>. That's roughly a third of all our fossil fuel emissions just being hoovered up by mushroom networks!
